summary.headline: UFO Moviez Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 43% YoY to ₹1,342 mn and FY26 net profit rose 161% to ₹249 mn, though Q4 EBITDA fell 13% QoQ.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 43% YoY to ₹1,342 mn and 2% QoQ, with EBITDA up 55% YoY to ₹182 mn but down 13% QoQ from ₹210 mn. Net profit was ₹45 mn, down 30% QoQ from ₹64 mn. For FY26, revenue grew 15% to ₹4,864 mn, EBITDA 36% to ₹803 mn and net profit 161% to ₹249 mn. Management attributed the strong March to Dhurandhar: The Revenge, while receivables and DSO rose sharply because much of that film's revenue was booked at year-end.

segments.name: Digital cinema advertising network
segments.commentary: Advertising footprint at 4,049 screens: 2,597 multiplex and 1,452 single. Management says it remains the largest multiplex screen advertising network in India.

segments.name: Caravan business
segments.commentary: Discontinued in FY26 due to inconsistent pipeline; old vans (over 10 years) were sold for about ₹2-3 cr. Company remains empanelled and may serve opportunities through third-party tie-ups.

guidance_outlook: Management is 'optimistic about sustaining growth momentum' with a healthy content pipeline and focus on advertising network and premium cinema initiatives.
Q1 FY27 started mixed with Bhooth Bangla, Raja Shivaji and Pati Patni Aur Woh Do; upcoming releases include Peddi, Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai, Welcome to the Jungle, Sarpanch and Cocktail 2.
Management expects ad-sharing ratio to gradually decline as revenues scale, since about 80% of revenue-sharing expense sits under minimum guarantee structures.
Management will provide DSO information for periods above 120 days in future quarters where a major film boosts year-end receivables.
Management says it intends to pursue both invested and non-invested (aggregated) advertising inventory models; activation and off-screen advertising initiatives are at an early, phased stage.
capex_capacity: Advertising footprint at 4,049 screens (2,597 multiplex, 1,452 single) as of the call.
Released 1,834 movies (including versions/languages) in FY26 vs 1,808 in FY25; 459 in Q4 FY26 vs 458 in Q4 FY25 and 457 in Q3 FY26.
Debt is raised mainly to fund expensive theatre equipment, typically via LC converted into loan, so debt movements are lumpy quarter to quarter.
Multiplex screens about 2,500 now vs about 1,000 when ad-sharing was 30-35%.
demand_pricing: Q4 box office: January strong (Ikkis, The Raja Saab, Border 2, Mardaani 3); February soft (O Romeo, Do Deewane Seher Mein); March strongest on Dhurandhar: The Revenge.
Q4 CDC and VPF revenues per screen declined YoY and QoQ because February was nearly blank and wide releases of Dhurandhar and Border crowded out other films; full-year CDC and VPF revenues grew.
Ad-sharing with theatres rose from the legacy 30-35% to about 59.5% because of multiplex mix and aggregated inventory where UFO did not invest; management says it is not losing pricing power.
UFO network delivered about 38% of footfalls for Dhurandhar and received about 30% of its ad revenue share, per management, using its ProCAT measurement tool.
Receivable cycle for ad sales is 110-150 days, up to 160 days depending on corporate or government clients.

qa_highlights.question: Why are employee and operating costs rising faster than revenue, and why keep the caravan business loss-making?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the employee cost rise is mainly variable pay (about ₹9 cr) paid this year after no payout last year. Caravan operations were shut down in FY26 and the vans sold for about ₹2-3 cr.

qa_highlights.question: Why have trade receivables risen so fast (₹162 cr vs ₹115 cr), and is DSO a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed the rise to higher ad revenue and a large Dhurandhar booking at March end. DSO was 147 days vs 121 in FY25 and about 134 in FY19; provisioning is adequate. Management agreed to show DSO for periods above 120 days in future.

qa_highlights.question: Is UFO losing pricing power as ad-sharing with theatres rose to about 59.5% from 33%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied losing pricing power. It cited multiplex mix, rental-linked minimum guarantees and aggregated inventory where UFO did not invest. It expects the ratio to decline as revenues scale.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue per screen fall in CDC and VPF in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said February was almost blank and blockbusters like Dhurandhar and Border drew wide releases, so other films avoided the window. Full-year CDC and VPF revenue still rose, and management says the business has stabilised.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of software, footfall monitoring and off-screen or activation initiatives?
qa_highlights.answer: Footfall and ProCAT are used to market the network to advertisers. Activation and off-screen advertising work has started but is at an early, phased stage.

qa_highlights.question: What was free cash flow, and why does debt rise while cash improves?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO did not give an FCF figure. Net cash rose from ₹48.3 cr to ₹59 cr despite about ₹15 cr tied in working capital including TDS. Debt is raised for theatre equipment via LC-to-loan conversions, and the company keeps both cash and debt by policy.

risks_watch: Receivables and DSO (147 days) could stay elevated if Dhurandhar-type year-end releases recur; watch for the new >120-day DSO disclosure.
Q4 EBITDA fell 13% QoQ and net profit fell 30% QoQ, so momentum is uneven quarter to quarter.
Ad-sharing ratio near 59.5% compresses margins; the company expects it to moderate as minimum guarantees are exceeded.
Employee costs rose to ₹94.7 cr; management says cost optimisation is ongoing.
Dependence on blockbuster timing: February was nearly blank and CDC/VPF per-screen revenue fell in Q4.
Q1 FY27 started mixed; success depends on the named Peddi, Welcome to the Jungle and Cocktail 2 releases.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability and the content pipeline, but defensive on receivables, ad-sharing and per-screen revenue. Management explained each concern with a structural reason and a commitment to add DSO disclosure, but gave no FCF figure or quantified cost-reduction target.
key_quotes: Q4 FY26 witnessed a meaningful improvement in theatrical momentum, supported by a stronger content pipeline and better audience engagement across markets.
Firstly, we are certainly not losing pricing power.
There is nothing concerning from a provisioning standpoint. Adequate provisions have been made wherever required.

adds.what: No new screens or capacity additions announced; advertising footprint stands at 4,049 screens (2,597 multiplex, 1,452 single)

growth.why: Management is only "optimistic about sustaining growth momentum" with no numeric revenue guidance; the Q1 FY27 slate is positive but mixed so far, and no capacity additions or capex were announced, so growth is backed only by content pipeline and the existing screen base.
